newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling slumps after IMF halts loan.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling slumps after IMF halts loan.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling slumped on Friday after an International Monetary Fund decision to halt a loan programme to Kenya amid demands for a crackdown on corruption.
"The Kenyan shilling opened at 59/59.50 versus the dollar and depreciated to 60/62.50 within 20 minutes," a dealer at Barclays Bank of Kenya told Reuters.
There were bids at as low as 64.50 from two leading commercial banks.
Kenya shilling slumps after IMF halts loan
Dealers said the market was very nervous and was awaiting a government reaction that would explain "where we go from here".

An IMF spokesman in Washinton said earlier that a $205 million three-year loan, offered under the IMF's Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility, would be allowed to lapse because the government's response to a July 24 deadline had been inadequate.

"The management of the International Monetary Fund has examined Kenya's request for an extension of the current (loan) and considers that the measures that the government is prepared to take fall short of meeting the clearly expressed concerns of IMF member countries in the area of governance," he said.
"Therefore the ESAF arrangement will lapse today."
